metadata.note: The Santa Fe Central Railway (1903-1908) and its successor the New Mexico Central (1908-1926), a 116-mile line from Santa Fe south through Kennedy (AT&SF crossing), Stanley, Moriarty, Estancia and Willard to Torrance on the El Paso & Southwestern / Rock Island Golden State Route, and the Atchison, Topeka and Santa Fe's 'Estancia District' remnant worked from Lamy via Kennedy after the AT&SF purchase. Features are split by operator (Rule 4) and, for the AT&SF era, by the pieces the line was cut into, since each has a different confirmed passenger span. Drawn spans follow research/branches/new_mexico_central_railway.txt 'drawable:' fields exactly.
metadata.omitted: Not drawn (drawable NONE in the research report): AT&SF-era Santa Fe - Kennedy and Willard - Torrance (no AT&SF passenger evidence; abandoned under ICC Finance Docket 6475, 1927, lifted c.1927-29); the Albuquerque Eastern's 8 graded/laid miles west of Moriarty (no evidence any train ran). The AT&SF years 1926-1935 on Kennedy - Willard are also undrawn: probable, unproven.
metadata.freight_only_audit: Nothing freight-only drawn: Willard - Calvert freight after the end of the mixed (after Jan 1951) to the 1972 ICC abandonment / c.1974 last train is excluded, as are the 1939 and 1942-43 abandonment years of Kennedy - Stanley and Stanley - Moriarty.
metadata.horsecar_audit: Not applicable: steam from 1903; the NMC's late Mack railbus is mechanical.
metadata.mileage_check: Whole line traced 115.4 mi vs 115.7 documented; Kennedy - Stanley 19.0 vs 19.3; Stanley - Moriarty 11.2 vs 11.7; Moriarty - Willard 27.9 vs 27.8; (undrawn as AT&SF) Santa Fe - Kennedy 22.0 vs 21.8 and Willard - Torrance 35.2 vs 35.7.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: [OPEN] end: Santa Fe: Moriarty - Willard - last confirmed passenger year 1951 (Feb 1952 Official Guide), actual end of the mixed unknown; [OPEN] start of the same feature at 1936 (AT&SF ran it from 1926/1924). [ANCHOR] 1936 only: Santa Fe: Kennedy - Stanley and Santa Fe: Stanley - Moriarty. New Mexico Central end drawn at 1924, the earlier bound of a 1924 (Fowler) vs 1926 (Wikipedia, abandonedrails, Re-Mike sheet) conflict over the AT&SF purchase date; Fowler's undefined NMC legend letter b might be the June 1926 Guide and would move it to 1926 - unverified. Exact first revenue train of 1903 and whether Santa Fe - Kennedy opened before Kennedy - Torrance are not established. Myrick, New Mexico's Railroads (UNM Press 1990) pp. 49-58 not consulted. Conflict: research/branches/atchison_topeka_and_santa_fe_railway.txt block [83] calls Moriarty - Willard 'Panhandle and Santa Fe' 1908-1951; this layer follows the NMC report (AT&SF, 1936-1951).
metadata.ownership_split: 1908 Santa Fe Central -> New Mexico Central (new company, new name: split). 1910 receivership and 1918 Railroad -> Railway reorganization: same road, not split. 1926 (Fowler 1924) AT&SF purchase: split; NMC Railway remained paper owner of the AT&SF-operated stub to 1972, not a further split.

properties.line: Santa Fe Central: Santa Fe – Torrance

properties.geometry_quality: Traced from OSM abandoned-railway ways via opstrace.py, 115.4 mi against 115.7 mi documented (Fowler NM sec. 31; '116 miles' per Wikipedia). Kennedy - Torrance is on OSM ways named 'New Mexico Central' / '"Frijoles Line" New Mexico Central' / old_railway_operator='New Mexico  Central' and an untagged railway=abandoned way (OSM 1390621564, 21.0 mi Moriarty - Estancia - Antelope) that continues the same grade; Santa Fe - Kennedy is on the named NMC/Frijoles Line ways 598933461 and 965486252 from a point ~4 mi south-west of the plaza. APPROXIMATED: (1) the Santa Fe approach, ~4.3 mi from Union Station south to the NMC grade at 35.640N, is drawn on surviving untagged rail (2.4 mi, the ex-AT&SF Lamy branch alignment now used by the Rail Runner / Santa Fe Southern) and the Arroyo Chamisos Trail (1.7 mi) - NOT identified in OSM as NMC track; the 1903 SFC's own approach into the railyard is not drawn and may differ. (2) Three straight-line bridges where the grade is not mapped: through Moriarty north of town 0.8 mi and south of town 0.6 mi, and at the Willard crossing of the Belen Cutoff 0.3 mi. No other straight legs. Era: the drawn grade is the 1903 alignment as surviving in OSM; no later realignment is known.

segments.note: Santa Fe Central Railway (renamed July 1901 from the Santa Fe, Albuquerque and Pacific), line Santa Fe - Kennedy - Stanley - Moriarty - Estancia - Willard - Torrance completed 1903 ('completed in August, 1903' per ahgp.org; exact first revenue passenger train not found). Local passenger service plus a through connection at Torrance with the El Paso and Northeastern / Rock Island. Shared Santa Fe Union Station with the D&RG from 1904. Fowler's 1906 working timetable (legend a) lists Donaciana, Vega Blanca, Progresso, Bianca and Torrance - 1906 is the independently proven year; 1903 is the completion year from two sources. Era ends 1908 at the consolidation into the New Mexico Central Railroad; trains continued under the new name. Daily headway is an unsourced estimate.
sources: Segment-level: 1903 completion per Wikipedia and ahgp.org Torrance County history; 1906 stations per Fowler NM sec. 31 (a = 1906w); 1908 consolidation per Wikipedia. Headway unsourced.

segments.note: New Mexico Central Railroad formed 1908 by consolidating the Santa Fe Central with the Albuquerque Eastern; in receivership from 1910, reorganized 1918 as the New Mexico Central Railway - the same operating road under the same display name, so not split. Mixed trains predominated, 'often as many cattle and sheep aboard as paying passengers'; in its final years a gasoline Mack railbus (motor rail car) carried passengers (Re-Mike sheet citing Glover, The Railroad Collection Vol. 1, 1977). Through connections at Torrance with the EP&SW and Rock Island. End 1924 is the EARLIER bound of a 1924-1926 conflict over the AT&SF purchase date (Fowler 1924; Wikipedia, abandonedrails and the Re-Mike sheet 1926); service probably ran to the sale, but only 1924 is drawn. Do not extend without evidence. Daily headway is an unsourced estimate.
sources: NOT SOURCED AT SEGMENT LEVEL: 1908 consolidation per Wikipedia and the 1924 end per Fowler NM secs. 7/31, but no NMC-era timetable year is confirmed for this segment; Myrick, New Mexico's Railroads (1990) pp. 49-58 not consulted.

segments.note: [ANCHOR] AT&SF Estancia District, worked from Lamy via Kennedy after the AT&SF bought the New Mexico Central (1926; Fowler says 1924). 1936 is the single proven AT&SF passenger year: Fowler's ATSF legend c = 1936 public timetable at Clark, Dyke, Trahey and Stanley. Service certainly ran wider in both directions - bracket is 1926 to the 1939 lifting of Kennedy - Stanley (ICC Docket 12191) - but no other year is confirmed. Do not widen without evidence. A daily mixed train; headway is an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: 1936 from Fowler NM PDF sec. 7 with ATSF legend c = 1936t; 1939 abandonment per ICC Docket 12191 via abandonedrails. Headway unsourced.

segments.note: [ANCHOR] AT&SF Estancia District. 1936 is the single proven AT&SF passenger year (Fowler ATSF legend c = 1936t at Stanley and Moriarty). Service certainly ran wider both ways - bracket 1926 to the 1942 ICC authorization (Docket 13831) and 1942-43 removal - but whether any passenger working reached Stanley after Kennedy - Stanley was lifted in 1939 is not established. No other year is confirmed; do not widen without evidence. Headway is an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: 1936 from Fowler NM PDF sec. 7 (c = 1936t); abandonment per ICC Docket 13831 via abandonedrails. Headway unsourced.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced from OSM abandoned-railway ways via opstrace.py (same grade as sfc-santa-fe-torrance), 27.9 mi against 27.8 mi (Feb 1952 Official Guide Table 45 '27.8 arr. Willard'; Fowler sec. 7; ICC AB-52 27.96 mi) documented. Moriarty on an unnamed abandoned way (1390621565), then a 0.6-mi STRAIGHT-LINE bridge south of Moriarty, then an untagged railway=abandoned way (1390621564, 21.0 mi, continuous with the named NMC grade) through McIntosh, Antelope and Estancia, the named 'Frijoles Line' NMC ways to Willard, and a 0.3-mi STRAIGHT-LINE bridge to the Belen Cutoff crossing at Willard. Era: drawn on the 1903 SFC/NMC alignment, the only one this piece ever had.

segments.note: [OPEN] at both ends. AT&SF mixed train Moriarty (renamed Calvert 1949) - Estancia - Willard, connecting with the Belen Cutoff at Willard. 1936 is the earliest CONFIRMED AT&SF passenger year (Fowler c = 1936t at Moriarty, McIntosh, Estancia); AT&SF operation began 1926 (or 1924) and earlier AT&SF passenger years are probable but unproven. 1951 is the last CONFIRMED year: Official Guide Feb 1952, AT&SF Table 45 'Moriarty and Willard', schedule dated 28 Jan 1951, Mixed No. 39/40, one train each way. This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - no source dates when the mixed actually stopped. Do not extend without evidence. Freight continued to the 1972 ICC abandonment (AB-52; last train c.1974) - an abandonment year, not a passenger end. Daily headway approximates one mixed each way; days of operation not legible.
sources: Segment-level: 1951 from Official Guide Feb 1952 AT&SF Table 45 (research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt) and its station index; 1936 from Fowler NM sec. 7 (c = 1936t); AB-52 via abandonedrails ICC filings.
